sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was raised materially: Q4 revenue guided to $65B ±2% versus $61.66B consensus, a massive raise. Management also claimed visibility to $500B in Blackwell+Rubin revenue through end of calendar 2026, and stated 'the number will grow.' The beat was organic (not attributed to one-time items), and management directly rebutted the AI bubble narrative with confident language. Deductions are minor: China revenue is zeroed out, and next-year margins are framed as 'try to hold' against rising input costs.

summary.revenue: $57 billion, up 62% year over year, with sequential growth of $10 billion or 22%.
summary.eps: Non-GAAP EPS $1.30 vs $1.25 LSEG consensus; GAAP EPS also $1.30.
summary.guidance: Q4 revenue expected to be $65 billion plus or minus 2%, implying 14% sequential growth at the midpoint. Management has visibility to a half a trillion dollars in Blackwell and Rubin revenue from the start of this year through the end of calendar year 2026.
summary.margin: GAAP gross margin 73.4%, non-GAAP gross margin 73.6%. Q4 gross margin guided to 74.875% respectively ±50 bps. For fiscal year 2027, management expects to hold gross margins in the mid-seventies despite rising input costs.
key_risks: China revenue constraints: 'Sizable purchase orders never materialized in the quarter due to geopolitical issues and the increasingly competitive market in China.'
Rising input costs: 'input costs are on the rise but we are working to hold gross margins in the mid-seventies.'
Inventory grew 32% quarter over quarter while supply commitments increased 63% sequentially.
Management is not assuming any data center compute revenue from China in the Q4 outlook.
key_opportunities: Data center revenue record $51 billion, up 66% year over year, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand.
Networking revenue $8.2 billion, up 162% year over year, with growth in NVLink, InfiniBand, and Spectrum X Ethernet.
Blackwell platform momentum: GB 300 contributed roughly two-thirds of total Blackwell revenue.
AI platform demand: 'The clouds are sold out, and our GPU installed base... is fully utilized.'
Strategic partnerships and investments with AWS, Humane, Suzuki, Intel, Arm, Anthropic, and others; up to 5 million GPUs associated with new AI factory projects.
Rubin platform on schedule for 2026 ramp, with first silicon delivered.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management directly rebutted the AI bubble narrative ('There's been a lot of talk about an AI bubble. From our vantage point, we see something very different.') and raised guidance materially, describing demand as exceeding expectations.
